questions.question: Which statement is FALSE regarding fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended during emergency
Some fundamental rights are negative in nature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended during emergency.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• Articles 20 and 21 are** **not the only fundamental rights that can be suspended during an emergency.
 
• **Other fundamental rights can also be suspended in certain circumstances.**
 
• Fundamental rights can be restricted by the state if it is necessary for the protection of** public order, morality, health,** or the rights of others.
 
• The Indian Constitution guarantees **six fundamental rights **to its citizens:
 
 
• right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental rights are justiciable, which means that individuals can approach the courts if their fundamental rights are violated.**
 
• Some fundamental rights are** negative**, which means that they impose a duty on the state to refrain from interfering with certain activities of individuals.
 
 
• **For example, the right to freedom of speech and expression is a negative right.**
 
 
 
• Fundamental rights can be suspended** **during an emergency, but not all of them.
 
 
• **Fundamental rights such as the right to freedom of movement, assembly, and speech can also be suspended in certain circumstances.**

questions.question: The Golden Quadrilateral connects which of the following cities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi-Kolkata-Mumbai-Chennai.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Golden Quadrilateral connects the cities of Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, and Chennai.**
 
• This highway network is approximately **5,846 km long **and was completed in **2012.**
 
• The project was initiated by the government of India in** 2001** with the aim of improving connectivity and facilitating trade and commerce across the country.
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral is one of the largest highway projects in the world and has helped to boost economic growth in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• These mega roads, which essentially encircle India, are primarily designed to shorten travel times between its major cities.
 
• **Other projects include the East-West corridor connecting Silchar (Assam) and Porbandar (Gujarat) and the North-South corridor connecting Srinagar (Jammu & Kashmir) and Kanyakumari (Tamil Nadu).**
 
• The **National Highway Authority of India** is in charge of carrying out these road developments.
 
• With a length of **5,846 kilometers, **it is the longest highway project in the world and the largest in India.
 
• **At a cost of ₹600 billion, it is the first phase of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) and consists of two, four, and six-lane expressways.**
 
• The project began in 2001, was planned in 1999, and was finished in July of 2013.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct about Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?

A) They are negative in nature.

B) They have moral and political sanctions.

C) They promote the welfare of the rich.

D) They are positive in nature.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**B and D.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are guidelines and principles laid down in the Indian Constitution for the government to follow while making laws and policies.**
 
• DPSPs are positive in nature, meaning they outline the positive actions that the government should take to promote the welfare of the people.
 
• **DPSPs have moral and political sanctions, which means that while they are not enforceable by the courts, they are still considered important principles for the government to follow.**
 
• DPSPs promote the welfare of all sections of the society, not just the rich.
 
• They aim to promote** social, economic and political justice,** and ensure equality of opportunity and status for all citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Directive Principles of the Irish Constitution, which address social fairness, economic well-being, foreign policy, and legal and administrative issues, served as the model for the DPSC's principles.**
 
• The following categories comprise Directive Principles:** Environmental, Justice and Legal, Political and Administrative, Economic and Socialistic, Peace and Security, and Monument Protection.**
 
• The concept of such policies "can be traced to the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen proclaimed by Revolutionary France and the Declaration of Independence by the American Colonies."
 
• The Universal Declaration of Human Rights by the United Nations has had an impact on the Indian constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated on the Makar Sankranti day in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magh Bihu.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Makar Sankranti is a Hindu festival celebrated on the 14th of January every year, marking the transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of Capricorn (Makar Rashi).**
 
• Magh Bihu is the festival celebrated on Makar Sankranti day in Assam.
 
• **It is also known as Bhogali Bihu or Maghar Domahi.**
 
• **Magh Bihu is a harvest festival and is celebrated with great enthusiasm and feasting.**
 
• It marks the end of the harvesting season and the beginning of a new agricultural cycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kati Bihu is celebrated in October/November and is also known as Kongali Bihu or Kangali Bihu.**

 
 
• It is celebrated during the sowing season and is a festival of prayers for a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Bohag Bihu or Rongali Bihu is celebrated in April and is also known as the Assamese New Year.**
 
 
• It marks the beginning of the Assamese calendar and the onset of spring.
 
 
 
• **Raksha Bandhan is an annual ritual or ceremony that serves as the centerpiece of the South Asian festival of the same name.**
 
 
• Sisters of all ages bind the rakhi, a talisman or charm, around their brothers' wrists on this day.
 
• They give them a present in exchange for their symbolic protection, and customarily give the brothers a portion of the duty for their possible upbringing.

questions.question: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was placed in the Guinness Book of World Records for which of the following achievements?

options.text: Opening the largest number of bank accounts in one month

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched in August 2014 by the Indian government.**
 
• **Its aim of providing financial inclusion and banking services to all households in India. **

• As of August 2021, the PMJDY has opened over 43 crore (430 million) bank accounts and mobilized over Rs 1.5 lakh crore (1.5 trillion) in deposits.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the reasons why the public sector played a dominant role in establishing the Industrial sector in India post-independence?

options.text: Poor savings capacity of the public
To avoid generation of private profit
Absence of large enough market for output
Lack of adequate capital with private industrialists

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** To avoid generation of private profit.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poor savings capacity of the public:**

 
 
• This was one of the main reasons why the public sector played a** **dominant role in establishing the industrial sector in India post-independence.
 
• The private sector did not have enough capital to invest in large-scale industries, and the government had to step in to fill this gap.
 
 
 
• **Absence of a large enough market for output:**
 
 
• Another reason why the public sector played a dominant role was that there was not a large enough market for the output of the industries.
 
• The private sector would have found it difficult to sustain their businesses in such a scenario, and the government had to step in to provide the necessary infrastructure and support.
 
 
 
• **Lack of adequate capital with private industrialists:**
 
 
• As mentioned earlier, the private sector did not have adequate capital to invest in large-scale industries.
 
• The government had to provide the necessary capital through various means such as subsidies, tax incentives, and loans.
 
 
 
• **To avoid the generation of private profit:**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because it goes against the basic principles of capitalism and entrepreneurship.
 
• The private sector is driven by the profit motive, and this is what encourages innovation, efficiency, and growth.
 
• The government's role is to facilitate this process by creating a conducive environment for businesses to thrive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial sector in India post-Independence:**

 
 
• The Indian government adopted a socialist approach to economic development after Independence in 1947.
 
• The focus was on building a self-sufficient economy through import substitution and state-led industrialization.
 
 
 
• **Private sector in India: **
 
 
• **​**The private sector was largely absent in the early years of Independence, as the government had nationalized many key industries.
 
• It was only in the 1980s and 1990s that the government started liberalizing the economy and allowing private participation in various sectors.
 
 
 
• **Public sector in India: **
 
 
• **​**The public sector played a dominant role in the Indian economy for several decades after Independence.
 
• The government set up various public sector enterprises in key industries such as steel, coal, power, and telecommunications.
 
• These enterprises were supposed to be the engines of growth and development for the country.
 
 

8c

questions.question: A diagonal relationship is found between which pair of the following elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Li and Mg.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lithium (Li) and Magnesium (Mg) show a diagonal relationship as they are located diagonally opposite to each other in the periodic table.**
 
• Both Li and Mg have similar atomic radii, electronegativities, and ionization energies due to the similarities in their electronic configurations.
 
• A diagonal relationship refers to the similarities in properties between elements that are diagonally opposite to each other in the periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diagonal relationship is a result of the similarities in the electronic configurations of these elements.**
 
• **Be and B do not show a diagonal relationship as they are not located diagonally opposite to each other in the periodic table.**
 
• Similarly, Be and Mg do not show a diagonal relationship as they belong to the same group and have different electronic configurations.
 
• Na and Mg also do not show a diagonal relationship as they belong to different periods and have different electronic configurations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a monetary policy instrument of RBI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government Spending.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• Government spending is not a monetary policy instrument of RBI.
 
• **It is a fiscal policy instrument used by the government to influence the economy.**
 
• **The bank rate is the rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks.**
 
• It is a monetary policy instrument used to regulate credit growth and inflation.
 
• Open market operations refer to the buying and selling of government securities by RBI in the open market.
 
• It is a monetary policy instrument used to inject or withdraw liquidity from the market.
 
• **The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the percentage of deposits that banks are required to keep with RBI.**
 
• **It is a monetary policy instrument used to regulate the money supply in the economy.**
 
• RBI uses a combination of monetary policy instruments to achieve its objectives of maintaining price stability, promoting economic growth, and ensuring financial stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government spending is a tool used by the government to influence the economy.**

 
 
• It refers to the amount of money spent by the government on goods and services, such as infrastructure development, social welfare programs, defense, etc.
 
 
 
• **The bank rate is an important tool used by RBI to regulate credit growth and inflation.**
 
 
• A higher bank rate makes borrowing expensive, which reduces credit growth and inflation, while a lower bank rate stimulates borrowing and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Open market operations are used by RBI to inject or withdraw liquidity from the market.**
 
 
• When RBI buys government securities, it injects liquidity into the market, while selling government securities withdraws liquidity from the market.
 
 
 
• **The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is used by RBI to regulate the money supply in the economy.**
 
 
• A higher CRR reduces the amount of money that banks can lend, which reduces credit growth and inflation, while a lower CRR stimulates credit growth and economic activity.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of investment?

options.text: Money spent on purchasing shares of a company
Machinery and equipment employed by a firm
Inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Money spent on purchasing shares of a company.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Investment is defined as the purchase of goods that are not consumed today but are used in the future to create wealth.**
 
• **In addition to residential construction, machinery and equipment employed by a firm, and inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm are all components of investment as they are used to generate future income.**
 
• Money spent on purchasing shares of a company is not a component of investment as it does not directly create wealth or generate future income.
 
• However, investing in shares can indirectly contribute to wealth creation through dividends and capital gains.
 
• It is important to note that investment can take various forms, including financial assets like stocks and bonds, as well as physical assets like real estate and machinery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Addition to residential construction: **This is a component of investment as it involves spending money on building or improving a property, which can generate future income through rent or sale.
 
• **Machinery and equipment employed by a firm:** This is a component of investment as it involves spending money on tools and equipment that can increase productivity and generate future income for the firm.
 
• **Inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm:** This is a component of investment as it involves spending money on goods that can be used to produce finished products and generate future income for the firm.
